verdict.text: The per-key lock closes the stale-write race the plan describes.
I found no path that can deadlock and no race in the map cleanup.
Both new tests check what their eval rows say.
Pass.
Gates: `loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree returned green (b2f3ede7...).
pre_commit, cli_tests and eval rows r1, r2 and r3 all passed.
Lock order: Apply takes the key after Resolve and before Limit.Wait, the S3 read and any tree lock.
It holds the key through Write (under RLock) or remove (RLock, then Lock).
Catch-up's direct remove takes its key outside any tree lock.
Catch-up calls Apply in sequence while holding no key, and nothing takes a key inside `remove`, `removeIfEmpty` or under `tree`.
So the waits only run key, then tree, then an OV slot.
A slot is held for one request only.
The graph has no cycle.
Map cleanup: `users` goes up under `k.mu` before the caller blocks on the entry's mutex and goes down under `k.mu` after unlock.
A waiter that arrives while the last holder is leaving either finds the entry (users > 0, so it is not deleted) or finds it already deleted and makes a fresh one.
Nobody can still be waiting on a deleted mutex.
r1: I copied the module to a scratch dir and removed the `defer c.keys.lock(uri)()` line.
TestApplySerializesPerKey then fails with `OpenViking holds "v1", want the latest content v2`.
With the fix it passed 5 of 5 runs.
The fixed 300 ms wait can only cause a false pass on broken code when the machine is slow (B has not finished its write within 300 ms).
It never causes a false failure on correct code, because with the fix B blocks no matter how long the wait is.
r2: TestPerKeyLockNoDeadlock runs folder removals (tree.Lock) at the same time as keyed writes and deletes, with catch-up looping.
It has a 60 s fatal timeout, then checks that OV converges and that the key map is empty.
It passed 5 of 5 runs.
Scope: catch-up can still remove a file after a stale listing (the delete-versus-recreate case).
The plan says catch-up already repairs that case, so leaving it out is right.
The CatchUp docstring and the .okf component sentences still match the code.
None.
The key is held during Limit.Wait.
That costs a worker slot only when two events for the same file are in flight at once, which is acceptable.
